name: /pace command — dynamic posting pace calculator
goal: Add /pace Telegram command (owner-only). Shows: posts recorded, posts remaining, days left to Apr 7, posts/day needed from today, today's target (ceil(remaining/daysLeft)), whether on track or behind. Also shows 'velocity' — posts per day average since first post (if any). Compact single message. Complements /queue (which shows which videos) — /pace shows the math of whether operator is on track.
rationale: 0/30 posts, 22 days. Operator needs a quick pulse check: 'am I on pace?' instead of doing mental math. /pace gives a one-line answer with today's target number. Drives urgency awareness without being verbose.
swarm: NOT USED — 2 file edits (commands.ts + index.ts) + 1 validation script. Direct write.

tasks.title: commands.ts — handlePace()
tasks.description:
handlePace(chatId, ownerChatId): owner-only gate. Reads workspace/scs001/manual-posts.jsonl to count recorded posts and extract timestamps. Computes: recordedCount, daysLeft = max(1, ceil((Apr7 - now) / 86400000)), postsNeeded = 30 - recordedCount. todayTarget = ceil(postsNeeded / daysLeft). rateNeeded = postsNeeded / daysLeft (to 1 decimal). If recordedCount > 0: compute velocity = recordedCount / daysSinceFirst. Status: if rateNeeded <= velocity: '✅ On track' else if velocity === 0: '🚨 Not started' else '⚠️ Behind pace'. Message format: '📊 Posting Pace — Apr 7 gate

✅/⚠️/🚨 Status: [status]
📹 Posted: {count}/30
📅 Days left: {daysLeft}
🎯 Need: {rateNeeded}/day
📌 Today: post {todayTarget} video(s)

(velocity: {velocity}/day avg since first post)'. Also add '/pace — Posting pace vs Apr 7 gate target (owner)' to handleHelp.
